items.claim: The 41:17-20 bound is warranted by a genuine second-to-third-person addressee shift, not merely by the weak parashah mark the row leans on in its own prose.
items.evidence: The preceding unit sustains direct second-person address to Jacob/Israel by name through web:Isa.41.14-Isa.41.16, naming the addressee and speaking of what that addressee will do; web:Isa.41.17 switches abruptly to third-person description of an unnamed group and a divine promise about them rather than to them. This byte-verifiable grammatical-person shift independently carries the opening boundary that the row's own topic-shift language under-articulates and that the cited PE mark (oshb:Isa.41.16, single-witness, tier-3) can only corroborate, never drive. The closing boundary is well-carried by the fresh judicial-summons formula opening web:Isa.41.21. The row discloses rather than hides the qadosh-Israel closing-title recurrence shared with the prior unit's own close, and gives a coherent reason (mark plus addressee shift) for keeping the units separate.

items.claim: The 41:21-29 trial-speech bound and its v.24-vs-v.29 close are correctly argued, and the row honestly discloses the 41:1 summons echo as a bracketing rival rather than suppressing it.
items.evidence: The opening double speaker-tag formula (says Yahweh / says the King of Jacob) and the closing PE mark match the marked-verse layer exactly at oshb:Isa.41.20 and oshb:Isa.41.29 (both single-witness). The paseq at oshb:Isa.41.22 and the ketiv/qere note at oshb:Isa.41.23 are present in the disclosure inventory exactly as cited, correctly count-only and non-adjudicating respectively. The rejected v.24 close is the real live rival (a verdict-only reading), correctly set aside because the second interrogation cycle in vv.25-29 continues to the actual PE-marked close. The summons idiom shared with web:Isa.41.1 is disclosed as an ABA bracketing rival around the intervening fear-not material rather than merged into it, which is the more defensible reading given the fear-not material's own distinct addressee and formula.

items.claim: The 42:1-4 bound is argued from a real tier-1 driver (the divine-frame onset at 42:5) rather than from the disputed servant-song convention, and the referent is correctly left undecided.
items.evidence: The closing boundary rests on the fresh koh-amar formula opening web:Isa.42.5, which independently belongs to the book's documented ha-El divine-frame class rather than being a bare content judgment; the PE marks bracketing the span at oshb:Isa.41.29 and oshb:Isa.42.4 match the marked-verse layer exactly (both single-witness). The mishpat inclusio between web:Isa.42.1 and web:Isa.42.4 is verified verbatim against the WEB text. The servant's identity is explicitly left open (individual, office, or corporate), consistent with the referent-never-decided constraint for this class of row.

items.claim: The divine-speech-frame formula opening 42:5 is correctly named as the ha-El variant rather than an unqualified koh-amar digit, and the strongest rival (extending the servant presentation through v.9) is honestly disclosed.
items.evidence: oshb:Isa.42.5's opening formula names God with the ha-El epithet, matching the book's documented list of non-adjacent divine-frame title forms rather than being treated as an ordinary undifferentiated koh-amar count. The PE marks bracketing the span at oshb:Isa.42.4 and oshb:Isa.42.9 and the paseq at oshb:Isa.42.5 match the marked-verse layer exactly (all single-witness). The addressee of the second-person commission in vv.6-7 is left open rather than assigned to the servant, the prophet, or Israel, and the rival reading extending the preceding servant presentation through v.9 is named as the real live alternative rather than a strawman.

items.claim: The 42:10-13 hymn bound is clean: correctly typed SAMEKH/PE brackets, a byte-clear imperative-onset genre shift, and a well-calibrated high confidence given the unit's clarity.
items.evidence: The opening PE mark at oshb:Isa.42.9 and the closing SAMEKH mark at oshb:Isa.42.13 match the marked-verse layer exactly (both single-witness, correctly not conflated with each other). The imperative hymn-call opening web:Isa.42.10 is a genuine grammatical and generic shift from the first-person divine commissioning speech that precedes it, and the first-person divine voice resuming at web:Isa.42.14 confirms the closing boundary independently of the parashah mark.

items.claim: The 42:14-17 bound is warranted by a genuine first-person divine self-declaration onset distinct in voice from the preceding hymn, with correctly typed SAMEKH brackets on both sides.
items.evidence: Both bracketing marks are SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.42.13 and oshb:Isa.42.17 (single-witness), matching the marked-verse layer exactly and correctly not conflated with PE. The first-person divine self-declaration opening web:Isa.42.14 is a clean grammatical-voice shift from the third-person imperative hymn-call of the prior span. The blind-guiding imagery shared with the deaf/blind servant address opening the following span (web:Isa.42.18-Isa.42.19) is disclosed as a cross-seam echo rather than silently merged, consistent with the addressee and grammatical-person shift at v.18's imperative onset.

items.claim: The refusal to atomize at 42:21-22 is well-grounded (no tier-1 marker opens v.21), and judgment_oracle correctly avoids deciding the unnamed servant's referent.
items.evidence: The opening SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.42.17 and closing PE at oshb:Isa.42.25 match the marked-verse layer exactly (single-witness); the two ketiv/qere notes at oshb:Isa.42.20 and oshb:Isa.42.24 are both present in the disclosure inventory as cited, correctly disclosed without adjudicating either reading. The rejected internal split at web:Isa.42.21-Isa.42.22 is the real live alternative, correctly set aside because no imperative, addressee shift, or divine-speech-frame formula opens v.21 in the bytes; the plundered-people material continues answering the same rebuke opened at vv.18-19. unit_type is judgment_oracle rather than servant_song, correctly declining to decide the servant's referent despite the strong unnamed-servant content.

items.claim: The 43:1-7 fear-not/creation-triad bound is well-carried on both seams; the mid-span qadosh-Israel occurrence at 43:3 was checked and does not function as an undisclosed bracket-closing device.
items.evidence: The opening PE mark at oshb:Isa.42.25 (single-witness) matches the marked-verse layer exactly, and the adversative onset plus fresh divine-speech formula opening web:Isa.43.1 independently carries that boundary. The two fear-not formulas (web:Isa.43.1, web:Isa.43.5) and the create/form/make triad closing web:Isa.43.7 are verified verbatim against the WEB text. The closing boundary is independently carried by the imperative addressee shift to the gathered nations opening web:Isa.43.8. The qadosh-Israel title recurrence inside the span at oshb:Isa.43.3 was checked against its syntax: it sits inside a causal clause naming God that continues the water/fire protection promise of v.2 into v.4's declaration of the addressee's worth, not in the verse-final capping position the same title occupies when it closes units elsewhere in this stretch of text; it does not argue against this row's bound and its non-disclosure does not weaken the row's warrant.
